articles.title: Margin Calculator
articles.summary: Cost, price, margin, markup, and profit math on any order page — with real per-unit costs pulled from inventory and a minimum-margin guardrail.

beginner.text: Press Ctrl+M on an order page (or use the Actions Shelf). The fields: Item Cost and Selling Price on the first row, Gross Margin % and Markup % below, then Qty, Unit Profit, and the animated Total Profit readout. Enter any two values and the rest compute as you type; Clear all resets.

beginner.title: Minimum margin guardrail
beginner.text: If the margin falls below your minimum (default 30%), the calculator flags it in red. Adjust the threshold under Settings → Developer Settings → 'Minimum allowed margin'.

intermediate.text: The calculator can pull live per-unit costs and stock levels for a SKU from the company inventory system. Costs are cached after the first lookup, and a bulk cost sync keeps the cost map warm.
Costs key on the human SKU (e.g. B3273). If a cost won't load, you may need an active session on the office portal — see the troubleshooting article.

articles.title: Charge / Refund
articles.summary: Run a credit-card charge or refund adjustment against an order without leaving the page.

intermediate.text: From the popup's ACTIONS section or the Actions Shelf on an order page, Charge opens a modal pre-loaded with the order's charge rows and the difference between the page total and what's been captured.
Review the rows, confirm or adjust the amount, and Run Charge. A spinner shows progress and a toast reports the result. Refunds use the same flow with a negative adjustment.
Charges are real money movements. The amount field pre-fills with the computed difference — always verify it against the order before running.

articles.title: Order Edit
articles.summary: Edit order details — dates, totals, notes — inline from the popup.

intermediate.text: The Order Edit button in the popup opens an in-page modal for adjusting order details and posting them back to the CRM in one step — useful for quick corrections that don't warrant opening the full order editor.

articles.title: Order Date Manager
articles.summary: Pick approval and commitment dates on two mini-calendars; saving runs the multi-step form chain for you with progress toasts.

beginner.text: On an order page, open Manage order dates from the Actions Shelf. It opens the Order Date Manager: two mini-calendars side by side — approval date on the left, commitment date on the right.
Pick both dates and click Update Dates. The save runs a multi-step process on the admin site; a step-by-step toast shows exactly where it is, and confirms when both dates are committed.

intermediate.text: The same Actions Shelf opens Quick Order Note, a keyboard-first picker and custom composer backed by your saved note templates. Apply last note repeats the most recently used saved template. Templates with Push dates forward configured route into the existing date-and-note push chain.
If a save fails mid-chain, the toast names the failing step. Nothing half-saves silently — re-open the calendar and retry.

articles.title: Quick Order Note
articles.summary: Apply a saved order-note template or compose a custom note from the Actions Shelf, with audience selection and optional date pushing.

beginner.text: On an order page, open the Actions Shelf and choose Apply order note. The compact modal starts as a searchable template picker. Pick a saved note to review it, or enter composer mode for a one-off note.

rows: Filters the note templates created in Manager → Notes.
Selects the exact audience value the order page expects.
The note content; saved templates can use {{date}} and {{time}}.
Routes the configured day offset through the existing date-and-note push chain.
Posts the note through the authenticated order-notes iframe.

beginner.text: After a saved template is applied, the shelf can expose Apply last note for a one-click repeat. This repeats the last saved template, not arbitrary free-form text.

intermediate.text: The Audience value in a template must exactly match an option on the order page. If it does not, review the template in Manager → Notes before applying it.
Date pushing uses the same multi-step calendar bridge as Order Date Manager. Progress and a failing step appear in toasts; a failed chain does not report success silently.

articles.title: Watch List
articles.summary: Your personal cross-session list of orders and contacts to keep an eye on, with priorities, due dates, and links back to each item.

beginner.text: Watch an order or contact from the popup's TRACKING section or the Actions Shelf — it lands on your Watch List with a link back to where it came from. Filter chips (All / Active / High priority / Completed) carry live counts, and the search box matches title, context, and due date.

items: A colored stripe on the left shows how long the item has been waiting: nothing (<1h), blue (1–4h), amber (4–6h), red (6h+). When anything goes red, the modal header tints red too and the subtitle counts the criticals.
Line one: priority dot + title. Line two: the context ('Order #29103', 'Contact #4421 · Marcus Chen', or 'Standalone') and the due date.
The right edge shows the item's age (5m, 2h, 3d); hovering swaps it for Edit and Remove buttons. The checkbox marks it done.

beginner.text: The Watch button (or Edit) opens the inline editor: title, priority (High/Med/Low), an optional due date, and the context picker — Standalone, or Order/Contact/Account with an ID (plus a name for contacts/accounts).

Completed items clean themselves up after 5 days (configurable in Developer Settings). The list is personal and stored locally — it isn't shared with the CRM or teammates. 'Clear all' asks for a second click to confirm.

articles.title: Copy Order IDs
articles.summary: Copy every order ID on the order index page to your clipboard in one click.

beginner.text: On the order index page, the Actions Shelf offers Copy Order IDs — one click puts every listed order ID on your clipboard, ready to paste into a report or spreadsheet.

articles.title: Signifyd Glow
articles.summary: Order rows on the index page glow according to their Signifyd fraud score, so risky orders stand out at a glance.

beginner.text: On the order index, the extension tints each row by its Signifyd fraud score — the stronger the warning color, the lower the score. The glow re-applies automatically as rows load, so it stays accurate while you scroll and filter.
Use the glow as a triage cue, not a verdict: open the order and check the actual Signifyd case before holding or canceling.
